CHAPTER: R.S.C., 1985, c. I-21
TITLE: Interpretation Act

1 This Act may be cited as the Interpretation Act.

2 In this Act, enactment means an Act or regulation or any portion of an Act or regulation.

3 Every provision of this Act applies, unless a contrary intention appears, to every enactment, whether enacted before or after the commencement of this Act.

4 The provisions of this Act apply to every enactment except to the extent that they are inconsistent with the enactment, and in interpreting an enactment
(a) every enactment is deemed remedial and is to be given such fair, large and liberal construction and interpretation as best ensures the attainment of its objects;
(b) an enactment shall be construed as being applicable to the circumstances as they arise; and
(c) the expiration of an enactment does not affect the validity of anything done or suffered, or any right or privilege acquired or accrued, under that enactment before its expiration.
